summary: Streaming requests with very large conversation history intermittently time out after heartbeat drop
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports streaming completions that begin successfully but fail mid-stream with a client-facing timeout after ~40-75s when the conversation history (system + user messages) exceeds ~120k tokens. Failures are observed only for dedicated tier customers on our us-east pool and primarily when max_tokens is set to a high value (>= 50k).

Impact:
- Affects Lexicon Labs production service: recurring failed streams for long-history sessions.
- Requests either close with a 504/timeout or a client-observed abrupt stream disconnect.
- Customer reports reduced completion reliability for long document synth jobs and increased error retries.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-lex-01 in us-east-1
- API: /v1/streams.generate over websocket + HTTP streaming fallback
- Models: redwood-13b-std (primary), redwood-7b-quant (fallback)

Steps to reproduce (as performed by customer):
1) Create a conversation with ~110-140k tokens of mixed system+user history across 12 messages.
2) Send streaming request with max_tokens=60000, temperature=0.7, stream=true.
3) Observe initial chunks streaming for ~20-40s then silence. Client reports heartbeat drop and ultimately times out at ~60-75s.

Observed logs/samples:
- Sample request-id: rwd-lex-20260310-8c12
- Upstream gateway logs show WS ping/pong activity stopped for the request at 00:00:40.
- Serving-runtime trace (trace id trace-9f3a) shows KV-cache reload and kernel scheduling for a large sequence window during same timeframe.
- No obvious 5xx from model container; model process remains alive.

Workarounds tried by customer:
- Lowering max_tokens to 8k avoids the timeouts.
- Requesting non-streaming generation works (though slower overall).

Desired outcome:
- Reliable streaming for very large contexts or clear guidance and server-side mitigations that avoid customer-visible timeouts.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: heartbeat/ping timeout triggered by transient backpressure when serving runtime performs KV cache eviction + kernel swap for extended token windows.

Findings so far:
- Websocket keepalive pings are sent from proxy at 15s intervals; pause correlated with long-running KV serialization tasks that block worker thread responsible for streaming flushes.
- Trace trace-9f3a shows a 28s blocking section during kv_append and slab reallocation that coincides with the missing ping window.
- Priority queueing in the serving runtime defers streaming flush work when large generation is scheduled with high max_tokens; this increases tail latency for streaming frames.
- Autoscaler and pool metrics: dp-lex-01 GPU utilization remained ~65%, but CPU threads on the model host spiked during these requests indicating host-side serialization overhead.
- No rate-limit logs or quota denial at gateway.

Repro steps executed by SRE:
- Replayed rwd-lex-20260310-8c12 in staging with identical payload and confirmed streaming silence at ~45s when KV size > threshold.
- Instrumented per-request flush latency and observed flush backpressure rising as prefix size grows beyond ~90k tokens.

Next technical actions planned:
- Add non-blocking KV append path to avoid blocking streaming flush thread (ENG-3121).
- Temporarily increase streaming proxy WS ping timeout for dp-lex-01 to 120s to reduce client-visible timeouts (short-term mitigation).
- Deploy prioritization change so streaming flush tasks are higher priority than background kernel selection when a streaming socket is open.
- Run load test across dp-lex pool to measure regressions and validate fix.

Logs and dashboards referenced:
- Grafana panels: serving.runtime.flush_latency, gpu.host_cpu_spikes, proxy.ws_ping_miss_rate
- Trace link: internal-tracing/trace-9f3a (available to ENG/SRE teams)
- Customer supplied raw client logs: attachment rwd-lex-8c12-client.log
resolution:
Mitigation applied: increased websocket keepalive timeout to 120s for dp-lex-01 and routed new long-history streaming requests to a patched worker class with non-blocking KV append.

Permanent fix plan:
- ENG ticket ENG-3121 created to implement a non-blocking KV append and to ensure streaming flush paths are isolated from heavy serialization work.
- Schedule rollout to all dedicated pools after bench validation and a canary in staging.
- Update docs and add a new Troubleshooting section in the Runbook about long-history streaming and recommended max_tokens defaults for dedicated pools.

Customer impact after mitigation:
- Lexicon Labs reported no new timeouts for two rolling days on requests that previously failed.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem to be filed if regression recurs.
- Add automated synthetic test that exercises >100k token prefix streaming to the CI gating for serving-runtime.
